summary: With no subplan you take the general Statistics MS: probability, stochastic processes, theory, applied statistics, linear algebra and programming courses, five 200-level STATS depth courses of 3+ units (independent study, research and workshops count only toward breadth) and three breadth courses. With the Data Science subplan you take its core, computational and machine learning courses, electives and a capstone instead. Both come to 45 units; required courses are letter graded, and courses below the 200 level count only for the named exceptions. Your 3.0 GPA, the program proposal, and the Data Science electives and capstone are checked by hand.

node.name: Statistics MS Depth Requirement
node.desc:
15 Units
Five (5) Statistics courses must be taken from graduate offerings in the Statistics department at or above the 200-level*.

*Statistics workshop (WKS), seminars (SEM), practicum (PRA), and independent research (INS, RES) credit (1-2 unit) may only count towards breadth/general elective credit. See Breadth section below.
*STATS 200Q is not an allowable course for graduate students.
node.notes:
• Must be taken for a letter grade, except those offered CR/S only.

• Course substitution may require DGS approval one quarter prior. Courses in the depth requirement must be STATS course or its cross-listing.

add.why: "15 Units / Five (5) Statistics courses must be taken from graduate offerings in the Statistics department at or above the 200-level*. *Statistics workshop (WKS), seminars (SEM), practicum (PRA), and independent research (INS, RES) credit (1-2 unit) may only count towards breadth/general elective credit ... *STATS 200Q is not an allowable course for graduate students." "Must be taken for a letter grade, except those offered CR/S only." "Courses in the depth requirement must be STATS course or its cross-listing." 1-2 unit credit is kept out by a 3-unit minimum. STATS 299 (Independent Study, up to 5 units, letter grade allowed) and the research and workshop courses STATS 298, 302, 398 and 399 are left out of the pool, since independent research and workshops "may only count towards breadth/general elective credit" whatever their units.

node.name: Breadth Requirement
node.desc:
Breadth courses are meant to complement their statistical training with graduate-level courses from a variety of disciplines. Courses develop relevant skills or emphasize applications of statistics and probability and expand their interests in areas such as optimization, scientific computing, economics, quantitative finance, healthcare, operations research, and environmental science.
Course substitution may require approval from DGS one quarter prior to enrollment.
node.notes:
Minimum three courses (3 units each).
Students can customize their academic experience through a wide range of elective courses in statistics and adjacent fields (lectures, workshops, training, independent study, practicum, seminars) enabling them to develop expertise aligned with their individual interests and professional aspirations.

• With the exception of STATS 118; Math 104, Math 113, Math 151; CS 106B, CS 107, CME 108, classes must be taken at the 200 level or higher.
May be taken for CR/S.
